segments.text: Netflix, Gmail, Swiggy, your bank's fraud alert. Almost all of it runs on just twelve machine learning algorithms.
segments.caption: Netflix, Gmail, Swiggy, your bank's fraud alert. Almost all of it runs on just 12 machine learning algorithms.

segments.text: Here's every one, explained in under three minutes. Save this before your next interview.
segments.caption: Here's every one, explained in under 3 minutes. Save this before your next interview.

segments.text: First, the map.
segments.caption: First, the map.

segments.text: Supervised algorithms learn from examples with answers. They predict a number, or a category. Unsupervised ones find patterns with no answers given. And reinforcement learning learns by trial and reward.
segments.caption: Supervised algorithms learn from examples with answers. They predict a number, or a category. Unsupervised ones find patterns with no answers given. And reinforcement learning learns by trial and reward.

segments.text: Number one: linear regression.
segments.caption: Number 1: linear regression.

segments.text: It draws the straight line that best fits your data. Bigger flat, higher rent. Use it to predict a number.
segments.caption: It draws the straight line that best fits your data. Bigger flat, higher rent. Use it to predict a number.

segments.text: Number two: logistic regression.
segments.caption: Number 2: logistic regression.

segments.text: Despite the name, it answers yes or no questions. It squeezes everything into a probability between zero and one. Will this customer buy? Eighty percent, yes.
segments.caption: Despite the name, it answers yes or no questions. It squeezes everything into a probability between 0 and 1. Will this customer buy? 80%, yes.

segments.text: Number three: decision tree.
segments.caption: Number 3: decision tree.

segments.text: A flowchart of yes or no questions. Salary above fifty thousand? Any existing loans? Approve, or reject.
segments.caption: A flowchart of yes or no questions. Salary above 50,000? Any existing loans? Approve, or reject.

segments.text: Number four: random forest.
segments.caption: Number 4: random forest.

segments.text: One tree can be wrong. So build hundreds, each on a slightly different slice of the data, and let them vote. Banks use it to catch fraud.
segments.caption: One tree can be wrong. So build hundreds, each on a slightly different slice of the data, and let them vote. Banks use it to catch fraud.

segments.text: Number five: gradient boosting, like XGBoost.
segments.caption: Number 5: gradient boosting, like XGBoost.

segments.text: Trees are built one after another, and each new tree fixes the mistakes of the last one. It wins most competitions on table data.
segments.caption: Trees are built one after another, and each new tree fixes the mistakes of the last one. It wins most competitions on table data.

segments.text: Number six: K nearest neighbours.
segments.caption: Number 6: K nearest neighbours.

segments.text: To label a new point, look at its closest neighbours, and copy the majority. You are who your neighbours are.
segments.caption: To label a new point, look at its closest neighbours, and copy the majority. You are who your neighbours are.

segments.text: Number seven: naive Bayes.
segments.caption: Number 7: naive Bayes.

segments.text: It counts how often words appear in spam versus normal mail. Free, winner, urgent? Probably spam. Great for text.
segments.caption: It counts how often words appear in spam versus normal mail. Free, winner, urgent? Probably spam. Great for text.

segments.text: Number eight: support vector machine.
segments.caption: Number 8: support vector machine.

segments.text: It draws the widest possible street between two classes. The points touching the edge of the street are the support vectors.
segments.caption: It draws the widest possible street between two classes. The points touching the edge of the street are the support vectors.

segments.text: Number nine: K means clustering.
segments.caption: Number 9: K-means clustering.

segments.text: No answers given. It drops K centres, gives each point to the nearest one, and moves the centres until the groups settle. Perfect for customer segments.
segments.caption: No answers given. It drops K centres, gives each point to the nearest one, and moves the centres until the groups settle. Perfect for customer segments.

segments.text: Number ten: PCA, principal component analysis.
segments.caption: Number 10: PCA, principal component analysis.

segments.text: It squeezes a hundred columns into a few that keep most of the information. Faster models, easier plots.
segments.caption: It squeezes 100 columns into a few that keep most of the information. Faster models, easier plots.

segments.text: Number eleven: neural networks.
segments.caption: Number 11: neural networks.

segments.text: Layers of tiny calculators, each passing signals forward. Stack enough layers, and you get deep learning: face unlock, translation, ChatGPT.
segments.caption: Layers of tiny calculators, each passing signals forward. Stack enough layers, and you get deep learning: face unlock, translation, ChatGPT.

segments.text: Number twelve: reinforcement learning.
segments.caption: Number 12: reinforcement learning.

segments.text: An agent tries actions, gets rewards or penalties, and slowly learns the best moves. That's how AI mastered chess and Go.
segments.caption: An agent tries actions, gets rewards or penalties, and slowly learns the best moves. That's how AI mastered chess and Go.

segments.text: So which one should you use? Predicting a number? Linear regression, or gradient boosting. Yes or no? Logistic regression, or a random forest. Finding groups? K means. Too many columns? PCA. Images or text? Neural networks.
segments.caption: So which one should you use? Predicting a number? Linear regression, or gradient boosting. Yes or no? Logistic regression, or a random forest. Finding groups? K means. Too many columns? PCA. Images or text? Neural networks.
